utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm afraid there could be some mistaken identity in what we just heard related to the name of Dragan Mirkovic. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It sounds as if Mr. Stojanovic is putting on evidence. I can talk with him outside the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because he asked for private session and we are not yet in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Stanojevic, your testimony has -- ends here, which means you're free to go. Our staff will assist you. On behalf of the Tribunal I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony, even though it was for such a short time, and on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to thank you too and all those present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just before the break, I asked you, Mr. McCloskey, to have further consultations with the Nikolic and Beara team on the Rule 68 material that the Defence teams submit exists and should be disclosed with urgency. Did you have further discussions with them?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I had brief discussions. Mr. Nikolic -- Mr. Nicholls and Ms. Nikolic had longer discussions and I heard they were fruitful but Ms. Nikolic would be better able to speak to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Nicholls and I discussed matters during the pause. We are waiting for fresh material that could be provided to the Defence in the course of the day, and I will then inform the Chamber of everything that has happened, and at latest, by tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we can adjourn the discussion on this matter to tomorrow morning. Yes, one moment. Shall we go through the tendering -- exhibit-tendering process relating to the last witness now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, from our list, I'm told that the only exhibit that we don't show having been already entered pursuant to 92 bis that was actually mentioned in his Blagojevic testimony is Exhibit 298, a vehicle log.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections on any one of the Defence teams to the admission of these documents, including the last one that has just been mentioned, Exhibit 298? We hear none, so they are so admitted. I don't imagine any of the Defence teams that have cross-examined this witness wish to tender any documents. All right. So the matter ends there. And the position is that you don't have any further witnesses after this one, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I saw you on the tip of your toes, thinking whether you should stand up and say something or not, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. It was -- I have no doubt in my mind, Your Honour, but I was just waiting for Your Honours to finish with the tendering of the evidence. During the break it appears that after discussing this with my client, it appears that there was some misunderstanding, maybe the discussion that I had with Mr. McCloskey before the Trial Chamber was a bit premature, and I would like just for the record to have -- to say that the position of Mr. Borovcanin's Defence remains the same as it was from the very beginning, so we are objecting to the admission of Mr. Borovcanin's interview, just however, I would like to have a clear situation of Mr. Borovcanin's Defence. So far, maybe this discussion took place prematurely because there is still no ruling on Prosecution motion to amend their 65 ter Rule list but this is how it was, and basically our position is the same as it was from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's how we understood it all the way, that any discussion that is were ongoing were of course without prejudice to the very first statement that you made in this courtroom, namely that you will be showing cause why this interview is not admissible in the first place. The discussion developed from there because it will be very difficult for any one of us to decide on objections to admissibility before we have actually had the opportunity to go through this interview in the first place. So we'll be coming back to you on this but I didn't want you or your client to get carried away with the idea that we considered your position as a contradictory one or that you had not made up your mind as to what it ultimately will be. I mean, we take it that throughout it has always been you're against having this interview admitted into evidence. All right. Tomorrow morning. Tomorrow morning, please do come prepared, as much as you can, to discuss the issue as to whether the Prosecution has a right to interview witnesses that have already been enlisted as Defence witnesses by any of the Defence teams. It's in relation to Popovic but I think -- the custom here has been one Defence team files a motion and then the other Defence teams fall in line with separate motions joining with the previous motion and so on and so forth. So I think if anyone wishes to contribute to the debate tomorrow, we have ample time for that. We have ample time for that. Yes, Mr. Meek, I see you wish to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Maybe a little guidance. You've just stated that any discussion as to in regards to the admissibility or the objections on the admissibility of this statement would be hard to make without actually reviewing the interview itself in the first place. I respectfully beg to differ. I believe that the threshold showing would be that the statement was given, it wasn't voluntary, it wasn't given knowingly, it wasn't given intelligently or there was some pressure, coercion, whatever it might be. Those issues can be addressed without getting into the substance of the statement itself. However, should Your Honours wish to have the statement in front of you, I will certainly make a motion, maybe it's premature, but anything in that statement that touches upon my client should be redacted and deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We haven't decided anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. We have made it clear that following an issue raised, I don't know whether you were here or not, but the matter was raised by Mr. Josse and the agreement is that those are issues that eventually will have to be debated, whether, in other words, a statement made by one of the co-accused has probative value in relation to other accused, et cetera. Of course, but those have got nothing to do with the admissibility issue as such, at least not for the time being, and we haven't actually agreed to what was submitted by Mr. McCloskey, and I think also agreed to by some of the Defence teams, that the admissibility issues will be addressed after we have had the opportunity to go through. How can you actually decide admissibility issues relating, touching on, for example, voluntariness, coercion, duress, independently of -- but anyway, we haven't decided that as yet and we will come back with our decision later. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think one of the things Mr. Meek may be touching on, it may just be how you would like us to set up the questioning, but there is a process, I think I remember, whereby we would ask a few questions of Mr. Graham, did you do it according to the rules, did you give him his rights, was there any promises or anything like that, very basic. And then it would stop and then the Defence, and this is -- might be asked or might have cross-examination on those issues without getting into the substance of the statement. Now, I don't know if you would like -- if that's what you had in mind, or that we just went all the way through with it. It can be done a number of ways and that may have been partly what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We obviously need to discuss this but I did remind you that the onus of proving that the statement is voluntary and that it is been taken in accordance with the law, rests with you, because you are tendering that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. And I don't want to belabour the point but I think maybe I've been misunderstood and I'm sure you're going to correct me if I'm wrong. If there -- during this process, if there is any possibility that the Chamber wants to look at the substance of the statement given, at that point in time, I don't believe it's appropriate for Your Honours to be able to look or hear anything that Mr. Borovcanin may have said about any other co-accused in this case, including my client. And that's where I'm coming from. Understand? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Point taken. We will be considering that. Yes, Mr. Meek -- Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I believe that should have been a matter for the joinder, the original joinder motion as well, many months ago, but I do not object to it being argued at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey says that may have been a matter for the joinder motion many months ago, and likewise, putting these statements and these tapes on the 65 ter list should have been an issue months and years ago also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need to stop it here. We will be meeting to discuss this issue and also prepare for tomorrow's debate. Tomorrow we'll reconvene at 9.00 and we will go on as long as needed within time the time allocated to us. Have a good afternoon.
